label: Ground ball back to the pitcher
teaching_point: Comebackers are the most common play a pitcher makes. Field it, turn, and throw.

label: Chopper in front of the plate
teaching_point: Catcher has to come out from behind the mask and make a barehand-or-glove play.

label: Ground ball to first
teaching_point: The pitcher covering first is the single most-missed play at this age.

label: Ground ball in the hole at first
teaching_point: 1B ranges right, so somebody else has to be at the bag — that's the pitcher.

label: Ground ball deep in the hole at short
teaching_point: Long throw. Set your feet — a rushed throw here is two bases.

label: Ground ball up the middle
teaching_point: Both middle infielders break. Call it early and loud so you don't collide.

label: Slow roller down the third base line
teaching_point: Charge it. Barehand on the run, throw from where you are.

label: Bunt down the first base line
teaching_point: Second baseman must cover first — the first baseman is charging the ball.

label: Bunt down the third base line
teaching_point: Shortstop rotates to third. Nobody is home if he doesn't.

label: Pop up on the left side of the infield
teaching_point: The fielder going back has priority over the fielder coming in.

label: Pop up on the right side of the infield
Pop up over second base
teaching_point: Center fielder beats both middle infielders to this ball. Let him have it.

label: Foul pop behind the plate
teaching_point: Mask off, find the ball, then throw the mask the other way.

label: Foul pop down the first base line
Foul pop down the third base line
Fly ball to right field
teaching_point: Right fielder has the longest throw to third. Hit the cutoff.

label: Ball in the left-center gap
teaching_point: Two-man relay. The trail man saves a run when the relay throw gets away.

label: Double down the left field line
Double down the right field line
Ball over the center fielder's head
teaching_point: Nobody panics. Get it in with two throws, not one heroic one.

label: Wild pitch or passed ball
teaching_point: Pitcher covering the plate is the play nobody practices and everybody needs.

label: Runner steals second
teaching_point: Pitcher must get off the mound and out of the throwing lane.

label: Over the left fielder's head
teaching_point: Two-man relay. The trail man exists because 11-year-olds throw the relay over the cutoff's head.

label: Ball rolls into the left field corner
teaching_point: Longest throw on the field. Nobody should try to make it in one.

label: Ball rolls into the right field corner
Off the fence in right-center
teaching_point: Second base is open on purpose. The trail man is the one who retreats to it.

label: Cut man throws behind the runner at first
teaching_point: This is why the second baseman covers first on a throw home. Free out, twice a season.

label: Cut man throws behind the runner at second
teaching_point: Runners round second hard and stop watching the ball. The cut man is the only one who can see it.

label: Rundown between first and second
teaching_point: Run him BACK toward first. A runner retreating can't advance if you drop the ball.

label: Rundown between second and third
teaching_point: Run him back toward second. Never chase him toward a base he wants.

label: Rundown between third and home
teaching_point: The one that decides games. Catcher runs him back to third; pitcher takes the plate.

label: First and third: throw through to second
teaching_point: Use it when you're ahead or the run doesn't matter. You are trading a run for an out.

label: First and third: pitcher cuts the throw
teaching_point: Same look, same arm slot. The pitcher is the one making the decision, not the catcher.

label: First and third: look him back, give up the base
teaching_point: The safest play and the hardest to teach. Giving up second beats giving up a run.

label: Pickoff at first
teaching_point: You don't need velocity, you need surprise. Quick feet beat a big arm.

label: Pickoff at second
teaching_point: Timing play, not a look play. Count it out together so you arrive with the ball.

label: Catcher back-picks at third
teaching_point: High risk. Only with a big lead off the bag, and only on a clean catch.

label: Strike three in the dirt, ball at your feet
teaching_point: If the ball is right there, tag him. A three-foot tag beats a ninety-foot throw every time.

label: Strike three in the dirt, throw to first
teaching_point: Step around the batter and throw from OUTSIDE the baseline, or you'll hit him in the back.

label: Strike three gets all the way to the backstop
teaching_point: Now it's a wild pitch AND a dropped third strike. Look at the other runners before you look at the batter.

label: Strike three in the dirt, bases loaded, two outs
teaching_point: Everybody is forced, including the batter. Step on the plate — do not throw anywhere.

label: Squeeze bunt with a runner on third
teaching_point: You have about two seconds. Everybody charges, the catcher clears a lane, nobody panics.
